findings.note: Broken grammar: the object should be in the accusative ("určuje farbu") and "zrakovej vnímania" mismatches gender/case (should be "zrakového vnímania"), so the heard question sounds ungrammatical to a native, though it remains answerable.

The film title "Sinners" was replaced by "Grešníci", which is not a Slovak word nor the film's release title (Slovak would be "Hriešnici", and the original "Sinners" should have been kept absent certainty); a player who says "Sinners" or "Hriešnici" is graded wrong, so the answer is unrecognisable.
The explanation repeats the invented title "Grešníci", so it no longer supports a correct answer and reinforces a non-existent film name for the player.
"soustavy" is the Czech form; Slovak requires "sústavy" — a native speaker would immediately hear this as Czech interference in the question.
The same Czech form "soustavy" instead of Slovak "sústavy" recurs in the explanation.

findings.span: Ako nazývate skupinu vrán, keď sa všetky spolu zdržujú, stádo, kŕdeľ alebo vražda?
findings.note: The item rests on the English collective noun 'a murder of crows', which does not exist in Slovak; as worded, the Slovak question asks what a group of crows is called in Slovak, where the true answer is 'kŕdeľ', so a knowledgeable Slovak player answers correctly and is graded wrong.
The explanation drops the source's 'English collective nouns' framing, turning it into a plainly false statement about Slovak and removing the only cue that the question is about English usage.
The option order is swapped relative to the source ('a flock, a herd, or a murder'), which does not match the source option sequence.

"Ginger" (cat) is calqued as "zázvorové" (of the ginger spice); Slovak has no such colour category — the established term is "ryšavé/oranžové mačky" — so the spoken question asks about a thing that does not exist and a knowledgeable player cannot recognise what is being asked.

findings.span: približne štyri z piatich zázvorových mačiek sú samce
findings.note: The explanation repeats the same non-existent "zázvorové" colour term while its first half says "oranžovú srsť", so it neither matches itself nor supports the answer in comprehensible Slovak.
The option values are ordinary words left in English while the question asks "Pravda alebo nepravda", so a Slovak player answering aloud cannot match the offered options.
The correct answer is still English "True"; a player who correctly says "Pravda" will be graded wrong.
The correct option key moved from a (Dunaj) to b (Vltava), so a player who correctly says the Danube is graded wrong.
The correct answer was changed from 'The Danube' to 'Vltava', which is factually false — the Vltava does not flow through Bratislava.

findings.span: Vltava preteká Bratislavou na ceste z Viedne do Budapešti.
findings.note: The explanation now asserts a false fact and supports the wrong answer instead of the Danube.

Uses the ordinal form "siedme" (seventh) with wrong case agreement instead of the cardinal "všetkých ostatných sedem planét", which a native speaker would immediately correct, though the count and the answer remain clear.
The correct answer was changed from "Gold" (zlato) to "Striebro" (silver), so a Slovak player who correctly says "Zlato" for the symbol Au is graded wrong.

findings.span: Značka Au pochádza z latinského argentum.
findings.note: The explanation now derives Au from "argentum" (silver) instead of "aurum" (zlato), which is factually false and reinforces the flipped wrong answer.
The Slovak question is not a question at all but a two-word fragment ('dry thistle') that both loses the entire source question and effectively names the answer, making the item unplayable.
The primary correct answer is left in English although Slovak has the established term 'stepný bežec' (present only as an alternative), so the expected spoken form is the foreign one.

findings.span: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
findings.note: The question is left entirely in English, so a Slovak player hearing it read aloud cannot understand or answer the item — it is unplayable.
The Godfather is known in Slovak as 'Krstný otec'; 'Krstný syn' means 'godson' and is a non-existent title, so a player who correctly says 'Krstný otec' is graded wrong.

findings.span: Repliku vyslovuje Vito Corleone vo filme Krstný syn.
findings.note: The explanation repeats the invented title 'Krstný syn' instead of 'Krstný otec', reinforcing the wrong answer key.
The unit was changed from kilometres to miles, so the stated answer is factually false and a player who correctly says "približne 11 kilometrov" is graded wrong.
The alternative answer likewise converts km to miles, so no correct spoken Slovak answer matches the accepted answer set.

findings.span: siaha približne 10,9 míle pod hladinu mora
findings.note: The explanation also replaces kilometres with miles, contradicting the source figure and reinforcing the wrong depth.
The established Slovak name is the feminine "Mariánska priekopa"; the masculine form is a wrong noun form a native speaker would correct.

findings.span: Prečo cibule robia teba plakať, keď ich sekáš?
findings.note: Word-for-word calque of "make you cry" — Slovak says "prečo z cibule slzia oči" / "prečo cibuľa vyháňa slzy"; the item stays understandable and gradable but reads as machine English.
Uses the stressed pronoun "teba" where Slovak requires the clitic "ťa" in this position, which no native speaker would produce.
The English subject pronoun "They" is carried over; Slovak drops it ("Uvoľňujú sírnu zlúčeninu…"), and the explicit "Oni" sounds foreign in the spoken answer the player must match.

"robí podráždenie" is a literal rendering of "makes irritation"; Slovak uses the verb "dráždi oči" (or "spôsobuje podráždenie očí"), so the graded answer string is unnatural and may not match a native player's phrasing.
Same calque repeated in the alternative answer, weakening the fallback string that is supposed to catch a natural spoken answer.

findings.span: ktorá robí reakciu s vlhkosťou v oku
findings.note: Calque of "reacts with"; Slovak requires "reaguje s vlhkosťou v oku", so the explanation reads as broken Slovak.
"sekať" suggests hacking/chopping wood rather than slicing an onion; the explanation itself uses "krájanie", so "keď ju krájaš" would be consistent and natural.

The German exonym Joachimsthal was replaced by the Slovak/Czech name Jáchymov, which is the correct answer — the question hands the player the answer outright and additionally states a falsehood (the German name is not "Jáchymov").

The band name Queen is invariable in Slovak and must not take a possessive-adjective ending; the correct form is "štvrtý štúdiový album skupiny Queen", and a native speaker would immediately mark "Queenina" as wrong.
The song title "Imagine" was literally translated; a Slovak player who knows the answer will say "Imagine" (the only real title, with no Slovak release title) and be graded wrong.

The Slovak established form of the animal's name is "vombat" (family vombatovité); the English spelling "Wombat" (also in "Črevo wombata") is kept where Slovak has a standard form, though it is pronounced identically so grading is unaffected.
The song title "Bohemian Rhapsody" — which is the correct answer — has been literally translated, so a player who says the real title aloud will be graded wrong.

findings.span: a) Bohémska rapsódia | b) Rozhýbeme ťa | c) Niekoho na milovanie | d) Radio Ga Ga
findings.note: Three of the four options are Queen song titles that must stay verbatim but were translated ("We Will Rock You" → "Rozhýbeme ťa", "Somebody to Love" → "Niekoho na milovanie"), so the spoken options no longer match the source titles and are unrecognisable to a player.

findings.span: Bohémska rapsódia bola na vrchole britského rebríčka
findings.note: The explanation repeats the invented Slovak title instead of the actual song name, reinforcing the wrong answer string a player must produce.
Slovak has the established word "toliar" for this coin; a Slovak player who knows the subject will say "toliar" aloud and be graded wrong against the German/English form "Thaler".

findings.span: sa skrátil na thaler, z ktorého angličtina prevzala slovo dolár
findings.note: The etymology chain in Slovak runs joachimsthaler → toliar → dolár; leaving "thaler" untranslated makes the explanation fail to name the answer in Slovak and reinforces the wrong answer form.
